title: Exposure contribution shares
note: Baseline Shapley values allocate h(x)-h(b), with b the marginal-median reference. Importance is the evaluation-distribution mean absolute Shapley value; shares divide this quantity by its sum over all candidate exposures. Shares sum to 100% within a fit. Their sign-free magnitude includes main and interaction contributions. True and fitted allocations use identical combinations and reference levels. Uncertainty across repetitions is summarized by SD and MCSE.

title: Recovery of effects at observed exposure combinations
note: Each point represents one fixed independently sampled exposure combination, relative to the common reference vector. The vertical coordinate is its mean estimate across usable repetitions; the diagonal denotes the true contrast. A deterministic subset of evaluation points is displayed. Variability, RMSE and interval performance are reported in the tables, to quantify individual-fit stability alongside mean prediction agreement. CLR comparisons use the same adjustment settings as the joint-effect figure.

title: Interaction significance and direction recovery
note: Left: Holm-corrected pairwise interaction detection. Right: correct significant directions after Holm correction of the full interaction grid. Rates are calculated per repetition; tables give uncertainty and wrong-direction rates. Additive CLR models have exactly zero four-point interaction contrasts.

title: Interaction-effect recovery
note: All other exposures are fixed at the saved marginal-median reference. The evaluation range for each exposure is the range of its saved joint-curve concentrations. These constructed combinations define fixed-background response targets; some combinations can have limited data support. The same saved fits and reference vector are used in all comparisons. CLR uses the outcome adjustment: correct-adjustment fits supply G1/G2 and misspecified-adjustment fits supply G3/G4. Rows identify exposure pairs and columns identify nuisance scenarios. Interaction is h(a,b,z0) - h(a,b0,z0) - h(a0,b,z0) + h(a0,b0,z0): departure from additivity on the log OR scale. Both concentrations vary independently over a rectangular grid. Points show true contrasts versus mean predictions across repetitions. Faint vertical segments show empirical central 95% repetition ranges, showing between-repetition variability. Both CLR exposure models are additive and predict zero interaction up to numerical precision; their points can overlap. This structural difference is distinct from nuisance-model robustness. Anchor rows and columns, which have identically zero contrast, are excluded from the scatter and aggregate errors. All remaining points, including genuine zero interactions, enter error summaries. Scales are common across scenarios for each pair.

title: Recovery of the joint exposure effect
note: All exposures follow their common marginal quantile, relative to the vector of marginal medians. Curves are means over usable repetitions. Shaded regions are empirical 2.5th–97.5th percentiles across repetitions, showing between-repetition variability. The reference point is zero by construction. CLR uses outcome adjustment, with each correct-adjustment fit supplying G1/G2 and each misspecified-adjustment fit supplying G3/G4. Failure counts and uncertainty metrics are reported separately.

title: Optimization convergence
note: The line is the median gradient magnitude at each recorded iteration; shading is the 10th to 90th percentile range among fits reaching that iteration. The horizontal line is the stopping gradient tolerance. Different objective functions are shown in separate panels.

title: Kernel distance-parameter boundary rates
note: Rates summarize unique fitted kernels. The null-exposure bar pools all null-variable parameters. These numerical diagnostics describe fitted smoothness and are separate from the variable significance tests.

title: Absolute relative errors on the odds-ratio scale
note: Errors are 100 times abs(exp(estimated log OR minus true log OR) minus 1). Boxes summarize finite evaluation-point-by-repetition errors. Whiskers follow the 1.5-IQR rule; individual outliers are omitted from display only. Overflow errors remain infinite in numeric summaries and are never clipped to improve performance. Means, medians and upper quantiles are reported in the tables. Monte Carlo uncertainty uses independent repetitions.

title: Quantitative odds-ratio recovery: G1
note: Crosses denote true ORs; colored points denote repetition-mean ORs. Horizontal segments connect the separately averaged pointwise 95% interval endpoints. Full contrast definitions, errors and interval performance are tabulated.

title: Identification rates for each active exposure
note: Identification requires a Holm-adjusted numerical quadratic-form tail probability below 0.05. Intervals are 95% Wilson Monte Carlo intervals across usable repetitions. Humidity acts through a temperature interaction, without a main effect.

title: Availability of estimates and tests
note: Counts refer to complete independent repetitions. Completed records include failures. Point, covariance and variable-test availability are reported separately. Selection is requested for KDR-CC G1 only. Failed and unavailable tests retain explicit status and availability counts.

title: Model configurations
note: N and L count complete matched sets. M is the number of Gaussian-kernel centers. Kappa is the coefficient penalty during outcome-supervised kernel learning. Lambda multiplies the normalized mixed-derivative penalty in final estimation.

title: Recovery of exposure contribution shares
note: Baseline Shapley values allocate h(x)-h(b), with b the marginal-median reference. Importance is the evaluation-distribution mean absolute Shapley value; shares divide this quantity by its sum over all candidate exposures. Shares sum to 100% within a fit. Their sign-free magnitude includes main and interaction contributions. True and fitted allocations use identical combinations and reference levels. Uncertainty across repetitions is summarized by SD and MCSE.

title: Accuracy of estimated exposure-effect contrasts
note: RMS bias is the square root of the mean squared pointwise bias across common evaluation points. RMSE averages squared error over repetitions and points before taking the square root. Both are on the log OR scale. MCSE for these aggregate measures uses deletion of one entire repetition. Correct-direction detection requires the nominal 95% interval to exclude zero on the true-effect side; exact zero-reference contrasts are excluded. Wrong-direction significant detection is also reported. Independent repetitions determine Monte Carlo uncertainty.

title: Accuracy of interaction-effect contrasts
note: Contrasts are on the log OR scale at a common marginal-median background. RMS bias is sqrt(mean over evaluation points of squared repetition-mean error). RMSE is sqrt(mean squared error over all usable repetitions and points). MCSE uses deletion of an entire repetition; the empirical SD is summarized on its root-mean-square scale. Identically zero anchor contrasts are excluded; other zero true effects enter the absolute-error summaries. Usable/planned counts are reported separately for each component. Independent repetitions determine Monte Carlo uncertainty. Fit scenario records the CLR adjustment fit and its original independent-repetition count. Interaction is defined by four function evaluations; additive CLR models have zero log-OR interaction by construction.

title: Detection of overall pairwise interactions
note: For each pair, the statistic is the mean squared four-point log-OR interaction contrast on the fixed evaluation grid. Its centered-Gaussian null distribution is a weighted chi-square sum computed numerically with covariance eigenvalues. Holm correction covers the four prespecified pairs within each fit; alpha is 0.05 . Wilson intervals quantify Monte Carlo uncertainty across independent repetitions. Usable tests are reported separately.

title: Recovery of significant interaction directions
note: A correct direction requires a nonzero true contrast, a significant two-sided contrast test and agreement with its sign. The corrected version applies Holm across all non-anchor grid contrasts of all four pairs in each fit. Rates first average within each pair and repetition, then across repetitions; MCSE uses whole repetitions. The interaction sign can differ across the grid. Overall pair detection and pointwise direction detection are distinct criteria.

title: Configuration-level contribution and interaction performance
note: Contribution share error is the repetition-average root mean squared percentage-point error divided by 100. Miss rates equal one minus corrected detection rates; direction errors use the pointwise Holm rule. Counts show available interpretation and interaction repetitions.

title: Estimated exposure distance parameters
note: Positive distance parameters control Gaussian kernel smoothness. Bound indicators use a 1e-6 tolerance on the log scale. Null variables have their own distance parameters.

title: Outcome-supervised kernel optimization
note: Each independent kernel initialization reports its objective, projected gradient, optimizer status and bound hits. Shared kernels appear once rather than once per nuisance scenario.

title: Numerical fitting and covariance diagnostics
note: One row per planned fit. Point convergence, interval availability, interpretation availability and recorded errors are separate fields. Penalized convergence is assessed by the objective gradient and scaled step; the unpenalized equation residual is reported alongside it.

title: Distribution of absolute relative odds-ratio errors
note: Error (%) = 100 * abs(exp(estimated log OR - true log OR) - 1). Distributional summaries pool evaluation points and repetitions. MCSE of the mean is computed across repetition-level means. No acceptance threshold or clipping of large errors is used.

title: Recovery of quantitative exposure-effect odds ratios
note: All contrasts and confidence limits are exponentiated log OR contrasts. Single-exposure P75-versus-P25 contrasts hold the other exposures at their reference; temperature uses P10/P90 versus its specified optimum. Joint contrasts change all candidate exposures simultaneously. Mean CI limits average the lower and upper pointwise limits separately. RMS bias and RMSE use log OR; absolute OR error is 100*abs(exp(estimate-truth)-1).

title: Computational time and storage requirements
note: Times are recorded elapsed seconds for individual components on the running hardware. Shared learning and nuisance components are reused. Row-level component sums describe a fit in isolation; actual total elapsed time is recorded in the run log. G-family reuse can reduce observed nuisance timings. Memory is the sampled process working-set maximum across the relevant stages. R may retain allocator memory between tasks. Cache is the measured working-cache size before removal. Missing measurements are reported as NA, never zero.

title: Availability of fixed-background predictions
note: Each row identifies one planned saved fit. Predictions require its saved coefficients and kernel or comparator basis. Pending fits, failed fits and missing model files remain explicit. Comparator fits are evaluated once per adjustment specification and repetition, then displayed in the corresponding G scenarios.

title: Mean identification and false-positive rates
note: Rates are computed within each usable repetition and then averaged. TPR uses eight active exposures; FPR uses the candidate null exposures and is undefined when none are present. Monte Carlo intervals use repetition-level rates. Usable and planned repetitions are shown. These are empirical operating characteristics of the regularized test conditional on the learned kernel.

title: Accuracy of single-exposure effect curves
note: Contrasts are on the log OR scale at a common marginal-median background. RMS bias is sqrt(mean over evaluation points of squared repetition-mean error). RMSE is sqrt(mean squared error over all usable repetitions and points). MCSE uses deletion of an entire repetition; the empirical SD is summarized on its root-mean-square scale. Identically zero anchor contrasts are excluded; other zero true effects enter the absolute-error summaries. Usable/planned counts are reported separately for each component. Independent repetitions determine Monte Carlo uncertainty. Fit scenario records the CLR adjustment fit and its original independent-repetition count. A single-exposure curve describes a fixed-background contrast, including any interactions at that background, rather than a unique main-effect decomposition.

title: Uncertainty estimation and interval calibration
note: Empirical SD is computed across independent repetitions at each fixed point and summarized by its root mean square. Model SE is summarized on the same squared scale. SE ratio is model SE divided by empirical SD; its reference value is one. Coverage is the average pointwise coverage of nominal 95% intervals and is a secondary assessment. Intervals condition on the independently learned kernel; approximation and regularization bias are assessed separately through their empirical errors and coverage. Empirical variability across repetitions can also include kernel learning. Width and coverage must be interpreted together with bias and estimation error.
